review_disposition: Keep the architecture and useful implementation. A finite correction to supported adoption/recovery/continuation paths is necessary; no new epic or general framework.

severity_meaning.P1: Correct before relying on the affected privileged/content-authority path. No production damage is asserted.
severity_meaning.P2: Concrete workflow, authority or recovery defect; implement a narrow fix rather than generality.

findings.title: Preserved-work fingerprint misses edited rename destinations
findings.basis: Source-confirmed integration risk; copied algorithm reproduced with real Git and files.
findings.consequence: Changed renamed-file bytes can retain the same signed expected content fingerprint and be adopted under the earlier review.
findings.required_change: Correct rename/copy identity capture and bind adoption to the actual retained source content.
findings.regression: Prepare a dirty rename handoff, edit its destination again without changing HEAD or status, and require public application to refuse stale content.
findings.scope_boundary: No general index, version-control replacement or promise of globally atomic external filesystem observations.

findings.title: Integration dependency is mistaken for ownership during delegated recovery
findings.basis: Source-confirmed query/policy mismatch; isolated SQLite effect-selection counterexample.
findings.consequence: Recovering a stopped integrator can select and quarantine a live producer workspace whose integration_task_id names that integrator.
findings.required_change: Derive authorized workspaces from actual task/dispatch/lane ownership and validate the complete continuation binding. Consumer relationships do not confer producer ownership.
findings.regression: Stopped integrator plus a live clean producer in the same run; recovering the integrator must leave producer workspace, dispatch, claim and leases untouched.
findings.scope_boundary: Do not replace this check with project-wide shutdown or automatic scope widening.

findings.title: An adopted isolated producer points its integration target at itself
findings.basis: Source-confirmed assignment and publisher lookup; isolated SQLite reproduction.
findings.consequence: Initial successor claim can pass, but final producer publication fails with integrator_lane_missing in the normal distinct producer/integrator topology.
findings.required_change: Derive or explicitly bind the intended successor integration task and validate that it has the correct destination ownership.
findings.regression: Adopt an isolated producer into a run with a real integrator, commit retained work, complete/publish, consume the artifact and qualify the destination.
findings.scope_boundary: No generalized early dependency delivery or scheduler rewrite is needed.

findings.title: Expired public recovery preflight hides an already committed canonical receipt
findings.basis: Source-confirmed public call order; copied HMAC/preflight check with a stub canonical receipt.
findings.consequence: After DB commit and a private receipt-write failure, public retry after expiry refuses instead of returning the existing result, despite the lower-level replay implementation.
findings.required_change: After authenticating target and principal, look up the canonical committed result before enforcing fresh-execution expiry. Keep genuinely unexecuted expired grants forbidden.
findings.regression: Fault after recovery commit, advance time beyond expiry, invoke public maintain_execution as the same operator, and assert one original canonical result with no second recovery.
findings.scope_boundary: Reuse the existing canonical receipt route; no new transaction/authorization framework.

findings.title: Exact continuation incorrectly depends on global lane ranking
findings.basis: Source-confirmed difference between selection and dispatch; isolated SQLite ranking check.
findings.consequence: An eligible requested lane head is reported as not_serial_lane_head merely because another same-role lane has a higher-ranked task.
findings.required_change: Use the requested lane's actual dispatch eligibility or membership in all eligible candidates, not the first globally ranked candidate.
findings.regression: Two independent ready lanes of one role; lower-ranked exact target must assess ready and be claimable through the returned public arguments.
findings.scope_boundary: Readiness remains an observation, not a reservation.

findings.title: Retirement outgoing-consumer protection misses typed prerequisites
findings.basis: Source-confirmed guard coverage; isolated SQLite pending-checkpoint consumer counterexample.
findings.consequence: An external pending task can be left dependent on an unfinished checkpoint of a task just superseded; the current two consumer queries do not see it.
findings.required_change: Protect unresolved outgoing dependencies using the existing supported typed relations, including checkpoint and alternative interface/barrier paths where affected.
findings.regression: External task waiting for a pending checkpoint owned by OLD must prevent retirement without an explicit valid remapping; preserve usable completed historical requirements.
findings.scope_boundary: Do not require a new dependency graph framework or forbid all historical references.

findings.title: Supersession preparation can initialize or restore a missing authority
findings.basis: Source-confirmed constructor path; no local/full product reproduction.
findings.consequence: The preparation command opens Service writable, which can initialize/migrate or restore a missing database from a snapshot before target eligibility is established.
findings.required_change: Open the authority read-only during preparation and fail on an unavailable/mismatched authority. Writing the separately issued private grant remains intentional.
findings.regression: Existing project metadata and snapshot but absent authority DB: preparation must fail without creating/restoring a DB or issuing a usable assignment.
findings.scope_boundary: This is not a ban on authorized application or an instruction to implement database recovery.
